Definition: Percentage of national population with access to electricity (grid or off-grid). This is the primary indicator of energy infrastructure availability for ICT. Based on World Bank/IEA Tracking SDG7 data, national statistical offices, or Afrobarometer surveys.
revision_notes: Original code 4 (75-89%) confirmed. The Tracking SDG7/World Bank WDI survey-based figure referenced in the original comments (63.9% for 2023) would in isolation map to code 3 (50-74%), but this figure is now dated. More current, authoritative sources supersede it: Rwanda Energy Group's official statistics report cumulative household electricity connectivity of 84.6% as of July 2025 (59.6% grid-connected, 25.0% off-grid/solar), corroborated by a subsequent REG announcement of 85.4% by end-2025, and a World Bank project document dated September 2025 independently reports 82.2% of the national population with electricity access. All of these recent, authoritative figures fall within the 75-89% band, so the original code stands on stronger and fresher evidence than originally cited.
revised_comments: Rwanda has achieved substantial progress in electrification, with roughly 82-85% of the population now having access to electricity through a combination of national grid connections and off-grid solar systems. Rwanda Energy Group reports cumulative household connectivity of 84.6% as of July 2025 (59.6% on-grid, 25.0% off-grid), while a World Bank project document from September 2025 reports 82.2% of the national population with electricity access. This reflects one of the fastest electrification expansions globally, up from around 6% in 2008, driven by sustained government commitment under successive National Strategy for Transformation plans, with a target of universal access by 2029.
